details.bug_title: Selected task cannot be removed or moved to Completed Tasks
details.observed_behavior: The Remove button and task-selection checkboxes are inside the /addtask form, reproducing the reported Remove Task form-routing bug.
details.expected_behavior: Selecting a task and clicking Remove should submit the selected task to the remove-task endpoint and move it from the active task list to the completed task list.
evidence: The application source contains the POST /removetask endpoint.
The view contains a form with action="/addtask".
The Remove button uses formaction="/removetask".
The task list contains checkboxes using name="check".
The Remove button is inside the same /addtask form that contains the task checkboxes.
HTTP validation did not return status 200: <urlopen error [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it>

diagnosis.bug_title: Selected task cannot be removed or moved to Completed Tasks
diagnosis.failure_analysis: The Remove button and task selection checkboxes are nested inside the same form that posts to /addtask. When the Remove button is clicked, the browser submits the form to /addtask, not /removetask, because the form's action attribute overrides the button's formaction. Consequently, the /removetask route never receives the selected task data, and the task remains in the Added Tasks list.
diagnosis.root_cause: The form containing the task list and the Remove button incorrectly uses action="/addtask". The Remove button's formaction attribute is ignored due to the surrounding form's action, causing the POST to /addtask instead of /removetask.
evidence: The form tag in index.ejs has action="/addtask".
The Remove button inside that form has formaction="/removetask".
The task checkboxes use name="check" and are inside the same form.
The /removetask route expects req.body.check to contain selected tasks.
Reproduction evidence shows the Remove button does not trigger /removetask.
diagnosis.proposed_fix:
Move the task list and Remove button into a separate form that posts to /removetask. Keep the add task form only for adding new tasks. Example:

Added Task

<% for(var i=0;i
  • <%= task[i] %>
    • <% } %> This ensures the selected tasks are sent to /removetask and processed correctly.
verification_plan: Start the server and navigate to http://localhost:3000.
Add a new task using the Add Task form.
Select one or more tasks from the Added Task list.
Verify that the selected tasks disappear from the Added Task list and appear in the Completed task list.
Check the network tab to confirm a POST request is sent to /removetask with the correct form data.
